column6: Intelligent Conversation System for Electrical Safety Inspection Knowledge Based on Deepseek
column7: To address key issues in electrical safety inspection services, such as low response efficiency in professional consultations, the hallucination tendency of large language models, and difficulties in multimodal knowledge management, this paper proposes an intelligent dialogue system for electrical safety inspection knowledge based on the Deepseek-r1:8B model. Employing a lightweight generation and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) collaborative architecture, the system achieves a balance between the accuracy of professional responses and deployment flexibility via a Three-Stage Retrieval-Augmented Generation (TSE-RAG) framework. This framework integrates a RoBERTa-TextCNN-LSTM intent recognition model, a BGE-M3 multi-strategy retrieval model, and a BGE-Rerank model to construct a multimodal knowledge base covering 16 typical requirement scenarios, while using the low-memory and high-efficiency Deepseek-r1:8B model as the generation core. Structured prompt engineering and a retrieval result evaluation mechanism are further adopted to mitigate hallucinations. Experimental results demonstrate that the system outperforms the baseline Deepseek-r1:8B model (without external knowledge) in terms of retrieval precision, as well as response accuracy, relevance, and professionalism. The system also exhibits strong adaptability to intelligent dialogue scenarios for electrical safety inspections in the power sector.

column6: DocMind: Conversational PDF QA with RAG
column7: Traditional keyword searches offer no understa–nding of the semantics of the documents being searched, and Large Language Models (LLMs) are prone to hallucinations, making the extraction of relevant information from large PDF documents problematic. In this paper, we present DocMind, which is a framework for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for conversational question answering on PDF documents. The system combines semantic document parsing with token-based chunking, sentence-transformer embeddings, and HNSW-indexed vector retrieval. To find the relevant context for a document chunk, a user query is embedded in the same vector space, and the document chunk is provided to an LLM for generating a cohesive answer. DocMind, unlike standard RAG systems, has multi-turn conversational memory and a transparency feature that indicates when an answer is not justified by the document the user uploaded. Our experiments show DocMind outperforms BM25 and TF-IDF by a large margin in the BERT F1 score, ROUGE-L, and the faithfulness metric. DocMind, by semantic retrieval, combines controlled generation to enhance information accessibility and reduce hallucinations while providing reliable, transparent, and domain-agnostic question answering.

column6: ServeXcel: Trust-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Document-Intensive Customer Service in Digital Banking
column7: The accelerated digital transformation of banking has fundamentally altered how customers engage with financial institutions, placing unprecedented pressure on customer service systems to deliver fast, accurate, and contextually grounded responses. While recent advances in large language models have enabled conversational interfaces capable of fluent natural language interaction, their direct deployment in regulated financial environments remains constrained by hallucination risk, lack of source traceability, and limited alignment with institutional knowledge bases. This paper presents ServeXcel, a trust-aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture designed explicitly for document-intensive customer service scenarios in digital banking. Unlike conventional chatbot systems, ServeXcel integrates dense semantic retrieval over verified internal documents with controlled generation mechanisms to ensure factual accuracy, explainability, and regulatory compatibility. The proposed architecture is implemented using an offline, privacy-preserving pipeline that combines vector indexing, lightweight transformer embeddings, and quantized generative models, enabling deployment in resource-constrained and compliance-sensitive environments. Empirical evaluation using real banking documentation demonstrates that the proposed system improves retrieval accuracy, reduces hallucination rates, and enhances user trust while maintaining low response latency. To enhance generalizability, the proposed framework is further analyzed with respect to scalability considerations and multiturn conversational extensions. Preliminary insights indicate that ServeXcel maintains robust performance under increased corpus sizes and conversational depth, supporting its applicability in real-world digital banking environments. The results indicate that trust-aware RAG architectures such as ServeXcel offer a viable and scalable pathway toward dependable AI-driven customer service in modern financial institutions.

column6: A Dual-Channel Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework for Intelligent Safety Production Accident Handling
column7: The investigation report on safety production accidents contains valuable experiential knowledge, but its unstructured format hinders the efficient knowledge reuse and intelligent decision support. The existing Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) approaches exhibit obvious deficiencies in this specific domain. Retrieval mechanisms that rely exclusively on semantic matching often neglect key structured metadata such as accident severity levels and industry sectors, leading to the suboptimal or irrelevant retrieval outcomes. Large Language Models (LLMs) are prone to errors when processing lengthy documents and lack traceability, which increases the risk of generating unreliable content or “hallucinations”. To address these issues, this research proposes an enhanced, domain-specific RAG framework tailored for safety production: Dual-Channel Semantic-Structural Similarity Matching RAG (DC-RAG). This framework leverages LLMs to perform multi-dimensional structured knowledge extraction from accident reports. The dual-channel retrieval mechanism synergistically integrates semantic similarity and structured metadata to achieve more relevant case matching. Subsequently, DC-RAG generates context-aware response recommendations based on the retrieved historical cases. Evaluation on the incident report dataset (with 98 reports for testing and 353 for historical knowledge base) indicates that, DC-RAG (comprehensive score: 0.73) outperforms both simple RAG (0.58) compared and LLM direct generation (0.69) in producing high-quality, context-relevant handling recommendations, verifying its effectiveness in intelligent security decision support.

column6: FedMosaic: Federated Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Parametric Adapters
column7: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) enhances Large Language Models (LLMs) by grounding generation in external knowledge to improve factuality and reduce hallucinations. Yet most deployments assume a centralized corpus, which is infeasible in privacy-aware domains where knowledge remains siloed. This motivates federated RAG (FedRAG), where a central LLM server collaborates with distributed silos without sharing raw documents. In-context RAG violates this requirement by transmitting verbatim documents, whereas parametric RAG encodes documents into light weight adapters that merge with a frozen LLM at inference, avoiding raw-text exchange. We adopt the parametric approach but face two unique challenges induced by FedRAG: high storage and communication from per-document adapters, and destructive aggregation caused by indiscriminately merging multiple adapters. We present FedMosaic, the first federated RAG framework built on parametric adapters. FedMosaic clusters semantically related documents into multi-document adapters with document-specific masks to reduce overhead while preserving specificity, and performs selective adapter aggregation to combine only relevance-aligned, non-conflicting adapters. Experiments show that FedMosaic achieves an average 10.9% higher accuracy than state-of-the-art methods in four categories, while lowering storage costs by 78.8% to 86.3% and communication costs by 91.4%, and never sharing raw documents.

column7: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has become an effective paradigm for alleviating hallucinations in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) by incorporating external knowledge. However, existing multimodal RAG methods still face two major challenges: (1) the lack of explicit structured knowledge modeling, and (2) inaccurate cross-modal retrieval and alignment. To address these challenges, this paper proposes MMKG-RAG, a unified framework that integrates Multimodal Knowledge Graphs (MMKGs) with a dual-stage retrieval mechanism for structured knowledge grounding and precise cross-modal reasoning. Specifically, we first construct an MMKG by extracting and aligning textual and visual entities and relations from multimodal corpora. Then, a question-aware multimodal retriever is designed to capture semantic relevance across modalities, followed by a graph-based multi-hop retriever to explore structured relationships and implicit dependencies in the MMKG. Finally, the retrieved multimodal knowledge is fused with MLLMs to guide grounded and interpretable generation. Extensive experiments on the E-VQA and InfoSeek benchmarks demonstrate that MMKG-RAG consistently outperforms state-of-the-art multimodal RAG methods, achieving 36.3% and 40.5% accuracy, respectively. Further ablation studies validate the contribution of each module in the proposed framework.

column6: A Handbook-Grounded Retrieval-Augmented Generation Chatbot for Family Planning: Comparative Evaluation of Qwen3-4B and Llama-3.1-8B
column7: This study presents a handbook-grounded Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) chatbot for evidence-based family planning question answering using the Philippine Family Planning Handbook (2023 Edition) as a closed knowledge source. The system employs page-aware PDF extraction, overlapping chunking, and a hybrid BM25–FAISS retrieval pipeline with cross-encoder reranking to assemble page-attributed evidence. A controlled comparison evaluates Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 and Llama-3.1-8B-Instant as generator backends within the identical architecture. Results across ten domain-specific queries show that Qwen3-4B outperforms Llama-3.1-8B in grounding quality and efficiency, achieving higher Faithfulness (4.875 vs. 4.444), perfect Answer and Context Relevancy (5.000 vs. 4.556), improved completeness (3.000 vs. 2.333), and stronger semantic alignment (BERTScore F1: 0.802 vs. 0.796). Safety analysis reveals a 0.0% hallucination rate for Qwen3 compared to 11.1% for Llama, while maintaining correct refusal behavior for out-of-scope queries. Qwen3 also demonstrates substantially lower latency (6.33 s vs. 42.55 s). These results indicate that generator selection significantly affects reliability and efficiency in clinical RAG systems, with Qwen3-4B emerging as the preferred backend for handbook-grounded family planning chatbots.

column6: Automated Scoring System for Written Tests Enhancing Retrieval Augmented Systems with Different Chunking Strategies
column7: In the vast growing education sector, the usage of AI plays a vital role in assessing academic performance. However, traditional grading methods come with misleading outputs and inconsistencies that can impact student's academic assessments. To enhance the effectiveness of a scoring system, a robust Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework is implemented to enhance the structure and functionality of the academic assessor. Implementation of different chunking methods is done with base ground truth data from 3 subjects, that are Biology, Physics, and Chemistry book. Chunking the data is necessary as it divides long texts into smaller, more efficient parts. Writers then proceed to embed, index, and retrieve the chunked data based on sample questions that are provided and output metrics such as accuracy, diversity, and top chunks created. In the process, semantic and Agentic Chunking methods stood out the most due to high accuracy and latency scores. Whilst being free to use, semantic chunking method performs well outperforming other free chunking methods. On the other hand, the Agentic Chunking method, whilst being the most efficient and has the best accuracy (90 %), has a token system that makes it not free to use.

column6: Hallucination in Retrieval-Augmented Generation is a Context Construction Problem: A Constraint-Driven Cross-Modal Framework
column7: Hallucination remains a major challenge in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), especially for domain-specific question answering over heterogeneous documents containing text, tables, figures, and OCR-derived content. This paper argues that hallucination in document-grounded RAG is strongly influenced by context construction: the quality, structure, and coherence of the retrieved evidence supplied to the generator. To address this problem, this work proposes L-DSRAG, a constraint-driven cross-modal retrieval and context construction framework that integrates structure-aware chunking, modality normalization, hybrid retrieval, graph-based expansion, table-aware grouping, cross-modal pruning, and constraint-driven context packing. Rather than passing independently retrieved top-k chunks directly to the language model, the framework treats context construction as a constrained evidence-selection problem under token and structural constraints. The system is evaluated against a traditional RAG baseline using a 100-question benchmark covering factoid, aggregation, table-based, temporal, multi-span, cross-modal, and negative/unanswerable queries. Four questions are intentionally unanswerable and are used to evaluate hallucination avoidance. Faithfulness and answer relevancy are computed over all 100 questions, while context recall and context precision are computed over the 96 answerable questions because the unanswerable questions contain no retrievable ground-truth evidence. Results show that the full proposed method improves faithfulness from 0.750 to 0.900, answer relevancy from 0.740 to 0.880, and context recall from 0.740 to 0.947. Context precision decreases from 0.737 to 0.693 over the 96 answerable questions, reflecting a tradeoff between retrieval selectivity and evidence completeness. Ablation results show that most gains come from structure-aware retrieval and table-aware context construction, while cross-modal pruning provides additional improvements by refining the final evidence context. The framework operates entirely with locally hosted components, including BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5 embeddings and a local Qwen3-14B generator, supporting privacy-preserving and API-independent deployment. These findings show that hallucination reduction in RAG can be achieved not only through stronger generators, but through more structured and selective evidence construction before generation.

column6: RIPE-II: Retrieval In-Place Poisoning Evaluation with Indirect Injections
column7: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) systems have enhanced the performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) by effectively addressing challenges such as hallucinations and generating irrelevant responses. However, integrating the RAG technique into LLMs introduces privacy risks and potential data leakage issues from the retrieval pipeline. Indirect Prompt Injections (IPIs) occur when hidden instructions inside retrieved documents slip into a model’s context as trusted evidence, exploiting weak guardrails in RAG systems and leading to unauthorized data leaks, ambiguous outcomes, and policy overrides. Existing defenses rely on brittle delimiter heuristics or limited retriever adjustments, leaving RAG systems vulnerable to adversarial directives blended seamlessly into retrieved content. In this paper, we present RIPE-II, a corpus-level benchmark that evaluates IPIs under a realistic content-poisoning threat model. RIPE-II constructs delimiter-free, position-aware poisoned corpora across multiple domains and includes both textual and visual injections. Our design explicitly models mid-document placement, chunking, truncation, and cross-component propagation, reflecting how enterprise RAG systems ingest and process content. We introduce a two-stage evaluation framework that separates retrieval exposure from generation-time compliance and distinguishes embedding-based similarity from semantic override using a calibrated LLM-based judge. Across biomedical, financial, scientific, open-domain question answering, including multi-hop reasoning and web passage retrieval settings, we find that poisoned documents can reach the final model context in up to 97% of queries and rank first in up to 94% of cases, showing that retriever and reranker choices substantially shape RAG security exposure. We further show that cosine-based attack scoring can underreport semantic compromise by more than 5×, demonstrating that lexical or embedding similarity alone is insufficient for evaluating indirect prompt injection risk.

column6: Reliable Information Retrieval with LLMs: Automated Analysis and Comparison of large PDF Documents
column7: In high-stakes professional settings like the insurance industry, extracting information from complex PDF documents is critical yet challenging due to document length and technical language. While large language models (LLMs) offer new opportunities for automating document understanding, their usefulness depends on output accuracy, transparency, and verifiability. In critical contexts, users must be able to trace information back to credible sources to reduce risks from hallucinations or misinterpretation. This research explores how LLMs can support reliable, transparent information retrieval (IR) from complex documents. We introduce five IR system variants designed to iteratively improve LLM outputs through better context preservation and fine-grained source attribution. These systems incorporate enhancements such as Markdown-based parsing, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and advanced document preprocessing. The final iteration integrates Multi-view Content-aware (MC) indexing, which supports semantically targeted retrieval using keyword, summary, and raw-text views. To evaluate performance, we develop a domain-specific benchmark with curated insurance documents, ground-truth answers, as well as performance metrics for assessment of the answer accuracy, hallucination rate, and source attribution precision. Results show that systems with content-aware chunking or MC-Indexing outperform earlier versions in accuracy and attribution, though with added complexity. Our findings highlight the value of structure-preserving preprocessing, targeted retrieval, and source transparency in developing trustworthy AI tools for document analysis. Future work may explore automated verification loops and user-guided retrieval to improve interpretability and reliability further.

column6: H2RAG: A Hub-Aware Hypergraph Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework for Multi-Hop Reasoning
column7: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) reduces hallucinations in knowledge-intensive tasks but often struggles with insufficient global context and fragmented evidence chains in cross-document multi-hop reasoning. Dense retrieval based purely on semantic similarity overlooks structural associations induced by entity co-occurrence, while existing GraphRAG systems typically require costly preprocessing and are vulnerable to hub entities in real-world corpora. We propose H2RAG (Hub-Aware Hypergraph RAG), a lightweight hypergraph-based retrieval and reasoning framework for multi-hop QA. Offline, H2RAG constructs an entity-chunk hypergraph and suppresses hub-induced noise via TF-SoftIDF weighting. Online, it performs semantics-gated hypergraph diffusion and integrates structural and semantic signals through entropy-driven adaptive fusion with scale calibration. Querycomplexity routing and topology-consistent reranking further balance efficiency and reasoning depth while improving evidence coherence. Experiments on HotpotQA, 2 WikiMultiHopQA, and MuSiQue show consistent EM/F1 gains and H2RAG avoids global clustering, potentially enabling cheaper updates.

column7: Bearing fault diagnosis is critical for rotating machinery safety, yet existing methods are inefficient, poorly generalizable, and lack interpretability. This study proposes a bearing fault diagnosis large model based on multi-agent collaboration and multi-RAG fusion. A diagnosis rule knowledge base is constructed, and a three-agent collaborative architecture is designed to suppress LLM hallucinations via specialized division of labor. A prototype system is developed and validated through a case study, achieving full-process closed-loop operation. This study provides a reusable technical paradigm for next-generation industrial intelligent diagnosis systems.

column6: Democratizing Financial Education: An API-Driven Platform Powered by Retrieval-Augmented Generation
column7: Addressing the critical gap in financial literacy requires scalable educational solutions that resonate with digital-native learners. This paper details an end-to-end system for delivering reliable financial education through an integrable conversational interface. Our architecture first uses a web scraper to automatically build a high-quality knowledge base from a trusted national portal. This curated data then grounds a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) conversational agent, a crucial step to ensure factual accuracy and mitigate Artificial Intelligence (AI) “hallucinations.” The entire service is exposed via a high-performance Application Programming Interface (API), transforming the tool from a standalone application into a versatile service. This API-first design enables seamless integration into diverse educational ecosystems, such as university websites, learning management systems, and mobile apps, creating a trustworthy and scalable AI-powered educational platform.

column6: In-Storage Acceleration of Retrieval Augmented Generation as a Service
column7: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) services are rapidly gaining adoption in enterprise settings as they combine information retrieval systems (e.g., databases) with large language models (LLMs) to enhance response generation and reduce hallucinations. By augmenting an LLM’s fixed pre-trained knowledge with real-time information retrieval, RAG enables models to effectively extend their context to large knowledge bases by selectively retrieving only the most relevant information. As a result, RAG provides the effect of dynamic updates to the LLM’s knowledge without requiring expensive and time-consuming retraining. While some deployments keep the entire database in memory, RAG services are increasingly shifting toward persistent storage to accommodate ever-growing knowledge bases, enhance utility, and improve cost-efficiency. However, this transition fundamentally reshapes the system’s performance profile: empirical analysis reveals that the Search & Retrieval phase emerges as the dominant contributor to end-to-end latency. This phase typically involves (1) running a smaller language model to generate query embeddings, (2) executing similarity and relevance checks over varying data structures, and (3) performing frequent, long-latency accesses to persistent storage. To address this triad of challenges, we propose a metamorphic in-storage accelerator architecture that provides the necessary programmability to support diverse RAG algorithms, dynamic data structures, and varying computational patterns. The architecture also supports in-storage execution of smaller language models for query embedding generation while final LLM generation is executed on DGX A100 systems. Experimental results show up to 4.3 × and 1.5 × improvement in end-to-end throughput compared to conventional retrieval pipelines using Xeon CPUs with NVMe storage and A100 GPUs with DRAM, respectively.

column6: Privacy-Aware Distributed RAG with Confidence-Aware Retrieval Routing
column7: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as an effective paradigm for grounding large language models in external knowledge. However, conventional RAG systems rely on centralized knowledge bases, raising privacy and scalability challenges when data is distributed across institutions or edge devices. We propose CARD (Confidence-Aware Retrieval Routing for Distributed RAG), a privacy-aware distributed RAG framework that enables efficient cross-node collaboration while limiting raw data exposure. CARD introduces four components: (1) a Local Evidence Confidence Score that determines whether local retrieval suffices, (2) a Privacy-Aware Retrieval Router that selectively queries remote nodes using only low-sensitivity representations, (3) a Node Expertise Profile for targeted node selection, and (4) an Answer Consistency Verifier that reconciles multi-source evidence to reduce hallucination. Experiments on four benchmarks show that CARD reduces communication cost by 62% compared to broadcast-based routing while maintaining task performance within 4.4 percentage points of the centralized upper bound.

column6: Knowledge Distillation in RAG: Enabling Small Models to Efficiently Leverage Large-Scale Knowledge Bases
column7: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) combines neural retrieval and text generation to improve factuality and reduce hallucination in large language models. However, large RAG systems such as Fusion-in-Decoder (FiD) and DeepMind’s RETRO are computationally expensive and challenging to deploy in low-resource or latency-sensitive environments, as also observed in recent studies on compressed contexts and efficient inference. This paper presents RAG-KD, a unified dual-stage knowledge distillation (KD) framework that transfers both retrieval and generation capabilities from large teacher RAG models to smaller students. Our approach introduces a retrieval– generation consistency loss aligning document- and token-level attribution, inspired by attribution-based interpretability methods. Extensive experiments on Natural Questions (NQ), HotpotQA, and FiQA demonstrate that our student models retain over 90% of teacher performance while achieving lower latency and smaller memory footprint. We further analyze robustness under noisy retrieval and interpretability of the distilled models.

column6: Integrating External Knowledge with LLMs: A Systematic Review of RAG Approaches
column7: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in natural language understanding and generation, exhibiting exceptional in-context learning abilities without requiring extensive fine-tuning. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as a promising paradigm to address these challenges by combining LLMs with information retrieval (IR) techniques. By leveraging external knowledge bases, RAG pipelines retrieve and incorporate relevant information dynamically, enhancing the factual accuracy and adaptability of LLMs. This paper provides an overview of the state-of-the-art methods for implementing RAG in LLMs, examining key components of the RAG pipeline, including data preparation, retrieval, reranking, and post-retrieval techniques. We aim to highlight how these components collectively enable LLMs to achieve greater reliability and flexibility, paving the way for more robust AI applications.

Traditional generative models, while capable of producing human-like responses, often struggle with factual accuracy and context retention. Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) presents a novel approach to enhance the performance of AI chatbots by combining the strengths of both retrieval-based and generative models. The paper focuses on the development of an AI-driven chatbot using a RAG framework, integrating the Zephyr-7b model, to serve the needs of the ICT Academy of Kerala (ICTAK). The chatbot is engineered to deliver precise and contextually relevant responses to user queries by integrating advanced language models with structured data extracted from the ICTAK website. The data, which was meticulously scraped and processed, ensures that the chatbot's knowledge base remains current and accurately reflects the ICTAK's services and operations. A critical challenge addressed by this work is the issue of hallucinations in large language models (LLMs), where models may generate seemingly plausible yet incorrect or irrelevant information. To counteract this, the paper employs various chunking methods that enhance the chatbot's capability to retrieve and generate accurate responses. This AI Chatbot incorporates cutting-edge techniques in natural language processing, including document retrieval, context compression, and re-ranking. This multi-faceted approach ensures that the chatbot not only provides accurate responses but also delivers them in a contextually relevant manner.

column6: RAG Based Interactive Chatbot for Video Streaming Services
column7: The proliferation of content within video streaming services presents a significant challenge for users seeking personalized recommendations and specific information. This research addresses this challenge by developing a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) chatbotn designed to enhance user experience through conversational AI. The primary contribution of this work is a novel Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture featuring a dual-retrieval system that combines semantic search for descriptive requests and structured queries for fact based inquiries. This approach grounds the Large Language Model (LLM) in a factual knowledge base, mitigating the risk of hallucinations. The system is engineered to handle empty data retrieval scenarios by dynamically relaxing search filters, ensuring a robust user experience. The effectiveness of this RAG approach was validated through a comprehensive set of automated evaluations. The system demonstrates high precision in ranked list retrieval with questions like "Recommend me the top 5 action movies with highest IMDb scores", achieving an average NDCG@k of 0.837. While the chatbot shows strong semantic understanding by achieving 91% accuracy with contextual clues such as "Which Batman movies are directed by Christopher Nolan?", its performance with more ambiguous, plot-only queries (59.5% accuracy) indicates clear opportunities for future refinement. These results confirm that the dual-tool architecture successfully combines the flexibility of semantic search with the precision of structured queries, paving the way for more intuitive and efficient content discovery on streaming platforms.

column6: Quality Outweighs Quantity: Advancing Medical Question Answering with RAG-MCP Muti-Agent LLM Framework and Curated Knowledge Databases
column7: Medical multiple-choice question (MCQ) answering requires specialized domain knowledge, multi-step clinical reasoning, and ability to discriminate among closely related distractor options. Current large language models (LLMs) frequently exhibit hallucinations, inconsistent reasoning patterns, and unstable performance when confronted with complex biomedical scenarios. This study introduces a structured multiagent framework integrating Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with Model Context Protocol (MCP) to enhance accuracy and reliability in medical reasoning tasks. The proposed architecture employs an administrator agent that performs domain-specific task routing and coordinates five specialized medical agents-Physiology, Pathology, Clinical Medicine, Treatment and Pharmacology, and Public Health-integrating their outputs through weighted consensus for final answer selection. Critically, this study demonstrates that knowledge database quality significantly outweighs quantity in RAG systems: curating high-quality question subsets from knowledge data yields substantially greater performance gains than utilizing entire unfiltered knowledge datasets. Evaluated on MedMCQA and MedQA-USMLE benchmarks using GPT-oss 21B and LLaMA 4Scout 17B base models without fine-tuning, the MCP-based multiagent framework achieves approximately 5% accuracy improvement (71-75%) over single-agent baselines (66-70%). Furthermore, employing only top-500 highest-quality curated questions in RAG knowledge database boosts accuracy to nearly 80%, representing $\boldsymbol{\sim} \mathbf{1 0 \%}$ overall improvement. Ablation studies confirm multi-agent consensus mechanisms provide 1.0-2.4% additional gains beyond retrieval augmentation alone, while scaling analysis reveals optimal performance at 11-13% curated knowledge data. These findings establish that domain specialization, structured agent collaboration, and strategic data curation collectively enhance both accuracy and interpretability in medical reasoning systems, offering practical pathway for deploying reliable clinical decision support without computationally expensive model fine-tuning.

column6: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation-Powered Chatbot for Air Force Policy and Logistics Compliance
column7: Recent personnel cuts mandated by the U.S. government have intensified pressure on U.S. Department of the Air Force (DAF) personnel and highlighted the need to reduce administrative overload. A specific challenge arises from the more than 11,400 regulatory publications that DAF personnel must comply with. To increase operational efficiency and keep up with the increased adoption of generative artificial intelligence tools the Air Force Research Laboratory developed the Non-Classified Internet Protocol Router Generative Pre-trained Transformer (NIPRGPT). NIPRGPT is a chatbot designed for use by U.S. Department of Defense personnel, capable of answering questions from uploaded documents through retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). However, NIPRGPT is slow, computationally intensive, prone to hallucination, and has a restrictive context window. To address these limitations, this work presents a lightweight RAG chatbot that employs semantic chunking, twostep retrieval with a bi-encoder and a cross-encoder, and a small language model (SLM) to generate human-like responses. The proposed system was evaluated on 71 regulatory questions drawn from five DAF publications, with both answer and citation correctness assessed by two researchers and an Air Force lieutenant colonel. An Intraclass Correlation Coefficient of $\mathbf{0. 8 0}$ showed high inter-rater reliability, and the system achieved 99.15 % of NIPRGPT's accuracy while delivering a 12.34 -fold improvement in response latency. These results demonstrate that lightweight RAG systems can substantially aid with the reduction of administrative overload within the DAF.

column6: Psychological Assistance Model Based on Fine-Tuning and Knowledge Base Technology
column7: Amid rapid digital transformation and rising societal pressures, student mental health challenges are becoming increasingly urgent, underscoring the need for effective intervention strategies. This study presents an intelligent psychological assistance model that integrates Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA).The model is grounded in a structured mental health knowledge base built from authoritative sources, including the DSM-5-TR and the Crisis Intervention Protocol, supplemented with high-quality counseling dialogues to ensure professional reliability. Experimental results show that the proposed model consistently outperforms both general-purpose and domain-specific baselines (e.g., MindChat, MentaLLaMA) across BLEU-4, ROUGE-L, METEOR, and affect alignment. Qualitative analysis further demonstrates superior linguistic fluency, logical coherence, and empathetic relevance.

column6: Structural knowledge fission: a novel RAG paradigm for mitigating hallucinations in power system LLMs
column7: Although Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is widely employed to mitigate knowledge hallucinations and reasoning deficiencies in general Large Language Models (LLMs) applied to power systems, current methodologies remain limited by their reliance on unstructured text chunks or simplistic Question-Answer (QA) pairs. Such low-density knowledge organization lacks explicit logical reasoning chains and negative sampling signals, impairing the model's ability to pinpoint critical information and exclude interference in complex professional scenarios. In response, this paper proposes a "Knowledge Fission" enhancement method based on domain-specific textbooks. Beyond mere text generation, we design a logic-enhanced structured transformation paradigm that leverages collaborative LLM techniques to reconstruct declarative textbook knowledge into structured multiple-choice questions (MCQs) containing stems, multi-dimensional distractors, detailed analyses, and standard answers. By incorporating competitive options and Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning, this approach significantly bolsters logical density and contextual coherence. Utilizing a heterogeneous knowledge base comprising classic Chinese and English power system textbooks, comparative experiments were conducted on the Qwen series models (0.5B and 4B parameters). The results indicate that deploying structured MCQs as retrieval units yields a substantial improvement in RAG performance compared to traditional open-ended QA retrieval. Notably, accuracy in complex intrinsic knowledge tasks increased by over 8% (from 87.13% to 96.04%). This approach not only resolves the limitations of traditional RAG in high-confusion contexts but also establishes a new paradigm for constructing high-quality knowledge bases in vertical domain LLMs.

column6: Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning for Offensive Security: Towards Robust LLM Agents for CTF Automation
column7: We present a retrieval-first reasoning-agent architecture for automating offensive cybersecurity tasks in the Capture The Flag (CTF) format. Our core hypothesis is that domain-specific contextual retrieval can stabilize large language model (LLM) reasoning under adversarial, multi-step challenges. To test this, we construct a bespoke retrieval corpus from scratch—excluding benchmark leakage—covering key CTF domains such as binary exploitation, reverse engineering, cryptography, and web vulnerabilities. Using FAISS indexing and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), our agent integrates this corpus with GPT-4o via a lightweight, tool-agnostic pipeline. Evaluated on NYU CTF benchmark [2], the RAG-enhanced agent achieves a 57.1% improvement in task completion over the vanilla GPT-4o baseline. Unlike prior work, which often depends on fragile tool orchestration, we demonstrate that focused retrieval alone significantly improves reasoning stability, reduces hallucinations, and enhances task-solving accuracy. Our threat model also considers prompt injection and contextual ambiguity, underlining the need for interpretable, corpus-grounded architectures in offensive reasoning.

column6: Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Turkish Historical Texts: The “Multilingual Paradox” in Embedding Models
column7: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in general-purpose tasks; however, they often suffer from hallucinations and a lack of factual consistency, particularly when processing politically and historically charged texts. While Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) offers a promising solution by grounding generation in external knowledge, standard architectures often underperform in morphologically rich languages like Turkish, a challenge also observed in Arabic contexts. This study presents the first comprehensive RAG benchmark for Turkish historical texts, utilizing “Nutuk,” a seminal political discourse by Mustafa Kemal ATATÜRK. To overcome data scarcity in this low-resource domain, a synthetic Question-Answering (QA) dataset of 600 pairs was constructed using Claude-3.5, a methodology validated for enhancing model performance in low-resource languages. 90 configurations involving 5 embedding models (BGE-M3, XLM-RoBERTa, LaBSE, MPNet, MiniLM), 6 chunking strategies, and 3 chunk sizes (128, 256, 512 tokens) were systematically evaluated across 54,000 individual tests. Experimental results reveal a significant “Multilingual Paradox”: despite being optimized for multilingual tasks, XLM-RoBERTa exhibited the lowest performance (MRR: 0.077), whereas BGE-M3 achieved state-of-the-art results (MRR: 0.379). This disparity is attributed to the contrastive learning objectives employed by BGE-M3, which provide superior semantic separation in vector space. Furthermore, statistical tests (Friedman $\chi^{2}=69.11, p\lt0.001$) confirmed that model selection is the dominant factor in retrieval performance, while the proposed “Keyword-aware” chunking strategy proved optimal for semantic integrity. This work provides a reproducible baseline and theoretical insights for historical RAG applications in nonEnglish languages. Scope. Although RAG includes both retrieval and generation, this benchmark is designed to isolate retrieval effects under a controlled generator and prompt. We report downstream generation metrics (e.g., ROUGE and BERTScore), while deeper generation error-mode analysis is deferred to future work. Data. column6: Joint Optimization of Secure and Energy Efficient Retrieval Augmented Generation for Mobile Edge Computing
column7: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) greatly mitigates hallucinations in large language models by grounding responses in external documents, yet its adoption on mobile devices is hindered by two intertwined concerns: (i) security, because poisoned passages cached by adversaries can drive the model to generate harmful outputs, and (ii) efficiency, because deeper retrieval and wider uplinks consume limited battery and spectrum. Existing RAG security studies overlook bandwidth and power budgets, whereas mobile edge offloading literature assumes benign knowledge bases. Bridging this gap, in this paper we introduce the Security Cost Ratio (SCR) as a unified metric that rewards lower attack-success rate per joule expended, and we design an optimization problem to jointly control retrieval depth, bandwidth and transmit power in the mobile edge computing environment. To tackle the non-convex optimization problem, we derive closed-form KKT conditions and an epigraph transformation that attain the global optimum for retrieval depth. We then utilize a quadratic-transform fractional programming technique in an alternating framework that converges for bandwidth and transmit power allocation. Simulations across various system parameters and environmental settings demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves up to 1.8× higher SCR and 50% lower attack success rate, while maintaining rapid convergence.

System performance was evaluated through both manual and automated metrics. Manual evaluation achieved an average score of 4.73/5 (94.6%) across relevance, accuracy, and faithfulness, demonstrating strong alignment with user intent and reliable grounding in regulatory context. Automated RAG evaluation produced context recall of 0.66, context precision of 0.72, and faithfulness of 0.74, indicating effective retrieval and hallucination suppression, though answer relevancy (0.45) suggested room for improvement in response alignment. Subsystem analysis further showed stronger performance in the retrieval engine (0.694) compared with the generation component (0.594).

column6: Ontology-Aware RAG for Improved Question-Answering in Cybersecurity Education
column7: Integrating AI into education has the potential to transform the teaching of science and technology courses, particularly in the field of cybersecurity. AI-driven question-answering (QA) systems can actively manage uncertainty in cybersecurity problem-solving, offering interactive, inquiry-based learning experiences. Recently, Large language models (LLMs) have gained prominence in AI-driven QA systems, enabling advanced language understanding and user engagement. However, they face challenges like hallucinations and limited domain-specific knowledge, which reduce their reliability in educational settings. To address these challenges, we propose CyberRAG, an ontology-aware retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) approach for developing a reliable and safe QA system in cybersecurity education. Cyberrag employs a two-step approach: first, it augments the domain-specific knowledge by retrieving validated cybersecurity documents from a knowledge base to enhance the relevance and accuracy of the response. Second, it mitigates hallucinations and misuse by integrating a knowledge graph ontology to validate the final answer. Comprehensive experiments on publicly available datasets reveal that CyberRAG delivers accurate, reliable responses aligned with domain knowledge, demonstrating the potential of AI tools to enhance education.

column6: SC-RAG-CoT: An Optimization Method for Robotic Instruction Generation
column7: Large Language Models (LLMs) based robotic instruction generation and control methods provide flexible and efficient solutions for autonomous robot decision-making with natural language interaction and task generalization. However, traditional LLMs struggle to adapt to the dynamic physical environments and address the ambiguity of natural language instructions. Therefore, a mechanism that integrates physical environment information and guides users to clarify specific needs through human-computer interaction is required. To this end, we propose the SC-RAG-CoT framework, which combines spatially constrained retrieval augmented generation (SC-RAG) and Chain of Thought (CoT) interaction for robotic instruction generation. SC-RAG-CoT employs SC-RAG to retrieve contextual information from spatial knowledge bases (e.g., spatial data, object attributes) to mitigate hallucinations caused by environmental dynamics. Additionally, CoT decomposes ambiguous instructions into multi-step reasoning chains. The reliability of instruction generation is improved through explicit verification of intermediate logic, and users are guided to gradually clarify their needs through interactive mechanisms. Simulation and ablation experiments demonstrate that the proposed SC-RAG-CoT strategy reduces average communication rounds by 2.6 and failure rates by $25.3 \%$ compared to traditional LLM-based methods in standardized test scenarios.

column6: IM-RAG: Multi-Round Retrieval-Augmented Generation Through Learning Inner Monologues
column7: Although the Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) paradigms can use external knowledge to enhance and ground the outputs of Large Language Models (LLMs) to mitigate generative hallucinations and static knowledge base problems, they still suffer from limited flexibility in adopting Information Retrieval (IR) systems with varying capabilities, constrained interpretability during the multi-round retrieval process, and a lack of end-to-end optimization. To address these challenges, we propose a novel LLM-centric approach, IM-RAG, that integrates IR systems with LLMs to support multi-round RAG through learning Inner Monologues (IM, i.e., the human inner voice that narrates one's thoughts). During the IM process, the LLM serves as the core reasoning model (i.e., Reasoner ) to either propose queries to collect more information via the Retriever or to provide a final answer based on the conversational context. We also introduce a Refiner that improves the outputs from the Retriever, effectively bridging the gap between the Reasoner and IR modules with varying capabilities and fostering multi-round communications. The entire IM process is optimized via Reinforcement Learning (RL) where a Progress Tracker is incorporated to provide mid-step rewards, and the answer prediction is further separately optimized via Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT). We conduct extensive experiments with the HotPotQA dataset, a popular benchmark for retrieval-based, multi-step question-answering. The results show that our approach achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance while providing high flexibility in integrating IR modules as well as strong interpretability exhibited in the learned inner monologue.

column6: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation Information System for the Oil and Gas Industry
column7: Research Context: The oil and gas industry relies on extensive and complex technical documentation, making manual information retrieval slow and inefficient for engineers and technicians who require quick and reliable answers for decisions. Scientific and/or Practical Problem: Generalist Large Language Models (LLMs) often struggle with specialized domains, leading to inaccuracies, contextual errors (”hallucinations”), and an inability to handle specific technical jargon. Proposed Solution and/or Analysis: This paper presents ”RAG Petrolês”an information system assistant built using RetrievalAugmented Generation (RAG) on ”Petrolês”, a collection of Portuguese theses and dissertations on the topic. It uses the IBM Granite model for embeddings, FAISS for similarity search, and a combination of the DeepSeek R1 and Mistral Small 3.2 LLMs to generate and refine answers. column6: Artificial Intelligence for Quantitative Finance: A RAG-Augmented Multi-Agent Framework for Robust Equity Strategy Discovery
column7: This paper introduces an AI-driven multi-agent framework for automated quantitative strategy generation and validation, integrating large language model (LLM) agents with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to enhance factual accuracy and research reliability. By grounding each agent's reasoning in a curated financial knowledge base, the framework mitigates hallucination risks, improves decision consistency, and provides transparent explanations of trading logic and risk characteristics. column6: The Challenge of Improving Critical and Scientific Thinking in Engineering Students Through RAG Systems Based on Validated Scientific Corpora
column7: Developing critical and scientific thinking in engineering students remains a persistent challenge in higher education. Traditional teaching practices in mathematics and physics often prioritize procedural knowledge over analytical reasoning, leading to limited reflection, superficial understanding, and low levels of engagement. This research-in-progress doctoral study explores the potential of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems-artificial intelligence models supported by validated scientific corpora-to enhance critical and scientific thinking in firstand second-year engineering students. Based on constructivist and deep learning theories, the study proposes a mixed-method quasi-experimental design that integrates technological mediation, ethical literacy, and active learning strategies. This paper presents the theoretical framework, research design, preliminary observations from pilot experiences, detailed evaluation instruments, strategies for monitoring AI biases and hallucinations, and expected contributions. The study aims to provide an empirical basis and ethical framework for the integration of generative AI in engineering education.

column6: An optimized method for retrieval-augmented generation towards multimodal knowledge bases in underground space
column7: The technical documents accumulated in the field of underground space engineering represent valuable knowledge assets. However, their multimodal (e.g., text, tables, diagrams) and unstructured nature leads to inefficient knowledge retrieval and utilization. Conventional methods struggle with complex, cross-modal queries, while using large language models (LLMs) directly for answer generation carries the risk of factual hallucinations and contextual incoherence, failing to meet the precision requirements of professional applications. To address these challenges, this study focuses on optimizing a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system for underground space. First, we propose a text segmentation method based on document logical structure, which divides text into semantic units according to headings and numbering, establishing a solid foundation for subsequent knowledge extraction. Second, we develop a prompt optimization mechanism with hybrid terminology injection (static glossary + dynamic corpus mining), significantly enhancing the system's ability to identify key entities and relationships. Furthermore, the system integrates a multimodal output function, enabling the generated textual answers to be automatically linked with and presented alongside original charts and diagrams, providing users with intuitive visual evidence. We constructed a domain-specific knowledge graph using a dataset of 300 weekly reports from a project and conducted a systematic evaluation with statistical significance tests. Experimental results confirm that the optimized system significantly outperforms conventional approaches and the unoptimized baseline across multiple metrics (answer faithfulness, relevance, context precision, context recall), with all improvements validated to be statistically significant (p<0.05).

column6: ATU-Tutor: A RAG-Based Socratic Tutoring System with Agentic AI Adaptive Assessment
column7: Large language models (LLMs) have great potential for educational tutoring, but hallucinations, poor curriculum alignment, and limited access to domain specific knowledge limit their application in academic settings. Retrieval augmented generation (RAG) is one way to overcome these shortcomings by anchoring model outputs to external sources. Still, most educational RAG systems are limited to single turn question answering and offer little pedagogical assistance. The paper will provide the design and assessment of the RAG enhanced LLM chatbot in Socratic tutoring and adaptive quiz generation at Arkansas Tech University (ATU). The system employs a hybrid retrieval pipeline with FAISS, BM25, and cross encoder re ranking on a knowledge base of 2,328 chunks from 17 open educational resources textbooks, as well as a retriever fine tuned on 929 domain specific query passage pairs. The Qwen3 8B model supports both tutoring and assessment. In tutoring mode, the system generates grounded explanations and Socratic follow up questions; in assessment mode, it generates curriculum aligned multiple choice and short answer questions with immediate feedback. The assessment of 14 questions demonstrated strong results in relevance, conciseness, contextual grounding, and resistance to hallucinations, with overall heuristic and LLM scores of 4.00/5. Lower scores in empathy and Socratic scaffolding indicate areas for future improvement. The findings show the potential of retrieval based tutoring and self adaptive assessment in a university specific curriculum.

column6: Enhancing information extraction from long document: utilizing LLM's prompt engineering for long document set generation
column7: Large Language Models (LLMs) face challenges such as outdated knowledge, generation illusions, and opaque reasoning processes. To address these challenges, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as a solution by integrating external knowledge bases. However, traditional RAG encounters bottlenecks when dealing with long documents, such as information loss, incoherence, and low query precision at the granularity level. To tackle these issues, a novel method based on prompt engineering for efficient extraction of information from long documents is proposed. Firstly, a prompt engineering-based document segmentation algorithm is introduced to enhance the model’s capability to handle long document inputs. Then, utilizing prompt engineering, long documents are transformed into structured long document datasets with hierarchical summaries, including titles, headings, abstracts, and keywords, highlighting key information points to enhance document understanding and retrieval matching efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate that this method significantly improves the quality and precision of information extraction from long documents, outperforming traditional retrievalaugmented generation paradigms, thus paving the way for the development of interactive question-answering systems tailored for multi-document, multi-knowledge point scenarios. This method efficiently locates relevant content in long document sets based on query semantics, providing precise responses.

column6: Domain Knowledge Graph Construction Approach Based on Large Language Models
column7: Current approaches for constructing domain knowledge graphs suffer from limitations such as reliance on manually defined rules, insufficient annotated data, and excessive dependence on domain experts, leading to inefficient processes and inconsistent quality. To address the above problems, this paper proposes a novel LLM-based framework for building domain knowledge graphs. The framework leverages the information extraction capabilities of LLMs to automatically identify core components of knowledge graphs—including entities, relational triples, and events — from unstructured text. To enhance performance on domain-specific data and mitigate knowledge hallucination, the framework integrates retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with external knowledge bases and incorporates a reflective case library. Additionally, it features a comprehensive error detection and correction mechanism, along with a redundancy processing module, ensuring the generated knowledge graphs are concise and reliable. To validate the effectiveness of our approach, comparative and ablation experiments were conducted on CrossNER, CrossRE, and SciERC datasets. Results show: on CrossRE/SciERC, relation extraction F1-scores reach $0.575 / 0.578$ ($13.2 \% / 10.1 \%$ higher than SAC-KG); ablation studies confirm RAG cuts hallucinations by $\sim 8 \%$ and the reflective case library improves error avoidance by $\sim 5\%$.

column6: Enhancing Security Requirements Coverage via RAG and Automated Feedback Loops
column7: The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into Software Engineering offers efficiency but may also introduce significant risks. In Security Requirements Engineering (SRE), generic LLMs frequently exhibit omission errors-failing to identify necessary security constraints-and hallucinations. While Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) mitigates factual errors, standard implementations rely on semantic similarity, creating a bottleneck that overlooks structurally necessary but semantically distinct security categories. To address this, we propose a specialized RAG framework designed as an automated Quality Assurance mechanism. Our approach integrates a curated OWASP Knowledge Base with a novel two-stage generation pipeline. Unlike single-shot RAG, our system incorporates a deterministic threshold-based feedback loop: it statically analyzes the initial output's coverage against the security taxonomy and triggers an adaptive compensatory generation to populate under-represented categories. We evaluated the framework on UniClass, a web application case study, across repeated executions. Empirical results demonstrate that the pipeline achieves a stable Mean Coverage of 72% across relevant security categories with a high Applicability of $\mathbf{8 1 \%}$, as verified by one project developer. By enforcing structural completeness before implementation, our approach serves as a critical QA guardrail for secure AI-driven development.

column6: Efficient GraphRAG via Community Embedding for Global and Reasoning-Intensive Question Answering
column7: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) enables large language models (LLMs) to answer questions without hallucinations by retrieving external knowledge. However, it still struggles with addressing global and reasoning-intensive questions. The recently proposed GraphRAG tackles these issues by organizing the knowledge base into hierarchical graph communities, but its retrieval mechanism results in high computational costs and overly generalized answers. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel community embedding-based GraphRAG framework comprising three key components: a graph community encoder that embeds community descriptions into dense vectors for efficient knowledge graph retrieval, a hierarchical retriever that leverages the communities’ hierarchy to balance abstract and specific information, and an iterative question processor that recursively decomposes a multi-hop question to enable multi-step reasoning. Experiments demonstrate that our method reduces token consumption by 96.7% compared to GraphRAG while achieving comparable performance, and it outperforms other state-of-the-art RAG approaches in terms of answer quality.

column7: Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate extensive potential in text generation, attracting significant user interest and finding wide applications. However, when faced with insufficient knowledge, LLMs may generate information that deviates significantly from factual accuracy, a phenomenon known as the "hallucination" problem. This issue not only diminishes the practical value of LLMs but also presents significant challenges to their further development. Retrieve-Augmented Generation (RAG) addresses this limitation by incorporating external knowledge retrieval to augment the LLM’s knowledge base. However, indiscriminate retrieval can introduce low-quality information, thereby degrading the overall performance of the model. To address these challenges, we propose a novel framework: Heuristic Iterative Multi-source Retrieve-Augmented Generation (HIM-RAG). By leveraging innovative prompt engineering, the framework exploits LLMs’ zero-shot reasoning capabilities and their extensive built-in knowledge bases to produce hypothesized understandings and inferences. HIM-RAG incorporates a heuristic iterative retrieval mechanism, employing an extended hybrid knowledge retrieval toolset—such as knowledge graph reasoning chains and web retrieval technologies—coupled with a Critic Language Model (Critic LM) to filter high-quality information highly relevant to the query. This approach enhances the performance of fact-based complex reasoning tasks. Additionally, a re-ranking module evaluates and prioritizes the generated answers from each iteration, selecting the best-quality response and avoiding overgeneration. This ensures the generated content remains highly relevant to user queries. Experiments on open-domain question answering, reasoning, and fact verification tasks demonstrate that the HIM-RAG framework, applied with two LLM variants, exhibits significant advantages in both accuracy and explainability.

column6: Trusted RAG: Enhancing Business Document QA Accuracy with Hybrid Retrieval, Reranking, and Faithfulness Verification
column7: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems improve the factual grounding of large language models by retrieving only the required relevant external knowledge during answer generation which basically means retrieving the data only from the provided corpus and no scope for the hallucination. However, existing RAG pipelines can often suffer from retrieval inaccuracies, weak passage prioritization, and unreliable faithfulness evaluation, particularly in business document question-answering applications, it can give answers not even present in the document, which is basically what hallucination means. This paper proposes Trusted RAG, a lightweight retrieval-augmented framework that combines hybrid retrieval using BM25 and FAISS, query-based reranking, and per-chunk faithfulness verification to improve answer reliability and faithfulness. The hybrid retrieval mechanism integrates both the lexical and semantic similarity using a weighted combination strategy and then re-ranking to prioritize the most relevant passages before generation. Unlike traditional approaches that compute faithfulness against concatenated contexts, the proposed system evaluates similarity independently across retrieved passages and selects the maximum relevance score. Experiments were conducted on business-domain documents collected from Wikipedia using qwen/qwen3-32b through the Groq API. The proposed system achieved a decent faithfulness across all evaluated queries with an average faithfulness score of 0.87 and a composite accuracy of 71.2. Comparative analysis demonstrates that the proposed hybrid retrieval and verification strategy significantly improves retrieval quality and reduces hallucination. The results indicate that retrieval quality and verification mechanisms are equally important as model selection in reliable business-domain question answering systems.

column6: RAG Security and Privacy: Formalizing the Threat Model and Attack Surface
column7: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is an emerging approach in natural language processing that combines large language models (LLMs) with external document retrieval to produce more accurate and grounded responses. While RAG has shown strong potential in reducing hallucinations and improving factual consistency, it also introduces new privacy and security challenges that differ from those faced by traditional LLMs. Existing research has demonstrated that LLMs can leak sensitive information through training data memorization or adversarial prompts, and RAG systems inherit many of these vulnerabilities. At the same time, RAG's reliance on an external knowledge base opens new attack surfaces, including the potential for leaking information about the presence or content of retrieved documents, or for injecting malicious content to manipulate model behavior. Despite these risks, there is currently no formal framework that defines the threat landscape for RAG systems. In this paper, we address a critical gap in the literature by proposing, to the best of our knowledge, the first formal threat model for retrieval-RAG systems. We introduce a structured taxonomy of adversary types based on their access to model components and data, and we formally define key threat vectors such as documentlevel membership inference and data poisoning, which pose serious privacy and integrity risks in real-world deployments. By establishing formal definitions and attack models, our work lays the foundation for a more rigorous and principled understanding of privacy and security in RAG systems.

column6: CardioRAG: Toward Trustworthy Medical Question Answering Through Hypothetical Document and Instruction-Aware Embedding
column7: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improves the factual grounding of large language models (LLMs) by combining retrieval with generation, but applying it in specialized medical domains introduces real friction. Domain-specific terminology, scarce supervised relevance labels, embedding-space mismatch across heterogeneous models, and hallucination risk all create problems that general-purpose RAG pipelines weren't designed to solve. CardioRAG is a domain-aware hybrid retrieval framework for cardiology question answering. It combines instruction-aware query encoding, hypothetical document generation, projection-based embedding alignment, and dense retrieval. The framework builds two complementary query representations. The first encodes the user query with INBEDDER to capture semantic intent, then projects it into the document embedding space of an INSTRUCTOR-indexed cardiology knowledge base — bridging the mismatch between heterogeneous embedding models. The second uses a fine-tuned SciFive generator to produce hypothetical cardiology answers under the Hypothetical Document Embeddings (HyDE) paradigm; these generated texts are embedded and aggregated into a retrieval-oriented representation. Both vectors are fused through weighted combination and used for FAISS-based dense retrieval. A pre-retrieval domain gate filters out-of-scope queries before retrieval and answer generation, which limits hallucination exposure on off-domain inputs. Experiments on a cardiology-focused subset of the MIRIAD dataset show that CardioRAG outperforms a standard dense-retrieval RAG baseline on faithfulness, completeness, and hallucination resistance. Gains in answer correctness are modest, but the results indicate that hybrid query representation and domain-aware filtering can meaningfully improve groundedness in specialized medical QA.

column6: IHILLM-RAG: a safe and private medical large language model based on intelligent hardware interaction and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
column7: Large language models (LLMs) have shown great potential in medical question answering and health management in the rapidly evolving healthcare landscape these days. However, even with domain-specific pretraining, LLMs may potentially hallucinate and produce factually inaccurate outcomes. In addition, in the field of healthcare, due to the different habits, backgrounds, and physical conditions of patients, it is necessary to strengthen user-oriented medical assistants, but there is relatively little exploration of personalized medical assistants based on LLM. In this study, we propose a medical assistant LLM that combines external medical knowledge base and intelligent monitoring hardware interaction, which is called IHILLM-RAG. On the one hand, we build RAG system through external medical knowledge base to improve the security and accuracy of medical assistant and reduce the phenomenon of hallucination. On the other hand, we design the human physiological signal monitoring chip as a ”human-machine interface” and carry out physical interaction with the human body and data interaction with LLM, so as to enhance the LLM’s learning and memory of the user’s own habits and improve the degree of personalization. We evaluated IHILLM-RAG on the important medical question-answering datasets, our experimental results demonstrate that IHILLM-RAG compares to the state-of-the-art open source models, the accuracy of the three datasets was improved by an average of 62.4%, 50.4% and 48.6%. Through this work, we provide a safer and more personalized method for healthcare which achieves a new paradigm of medical consultation with ”Private AI-doctor” at any time and anywhere.

column6: Add-Rag: Agent-Driven Dynamic Rag with Adaptive Retrieval Strategies and Multi-Retriever Collaboration for Enhanced Generation
column7: Currently, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is employed to mitigate the hallucination issue in Large Language Models (LLMs) during knowledge retrieval, by integrating external knowledge bases. However, it also exposes several problems, such as relatively fixed retrieval strategies and overly simplistic feedback mechanisms. To address these issues, we propose a highly lightweight agent capable of dynamically selecting appropriate retrievers and adjusting retrieval parameters in response to changes in the retrieved content, thereby substantially improving retrieval efficiency. Moreover, the framework allows for the customization of task-specific retrieval strategy spaces to meet diverse application requirements. During training, we introduce a multi-dimensional reward mechanism—comprising retrieval strategy rewards, re-retrieval advantage rewards, and policy rewards—into the agent to enhance its ability to determine optimal retriever selection and configure retrieval parameters. For queries of varying difficulty, we have developed a cross-retrieval approach that utilizes multiple cooperating retrievers. For re-retrieval, we will also re-adjust the retrieval strategy to adapt to the new retrieved content. We evaluated the framework on multiple datasets and conducted ablation studies to verify the effectiveness of our method.

column6: MedPolicy-RAG: A Multi-Domain AI Chatbot for Healthcare Compliance Interpretation
column7: This paper presents a domain-aware multilingual Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework designed for regulatory document interpretation across five policy domains, including healthcare delivery, research funding, digital health data, food safety, and administrative directives. The proposed system supports both English and Devanagari Hindi documents and integrates optical character recognition (OCR) with dynamic language detection using the Google Vision API to process scanned and poorly formatted documents. Cross-lingual transformer embeddings enable semantic retrieval across languages, while a domain-aware routing mechanism restricts retrieval to relevant policy corpora, thereby reducing retrieval noise. A hybrid retrieval strategy combining dense vector search with cross-encoder and decoder-based re-ranking is employed to improve relevance, mitigate hallucination, and strengthen evidence grounding. The framework generates citation-aware responses in the user’s preferred language using structured prompting. Experimental evaluation on a gold-standard question-answer dataset demonstrates improved retrieval accuracy and answer fidelity compared with monolingual retrieval and conventional RAG baselines, establishing the framework as an effective multi-lingual regulatory assistant for the Indian healthcare and public policy environments.

column6: RACG-DRT: Retrieval Augumented Code Generation Based on Dynamic Revision of Thoughts
column7: Large models have the problems of hallucinations in the field of code generation. The causes of these hallucinations include errors in the model’s reasoning process, inadequate overall knowledge, and insufficient localized knowledge. To tackle these challenges, the prevailing approach currently involves influencing the large model’s reasoning and prediction processes through techniques such as chain of thought, single-shot retrievalaugmented generation, and dynamic retrieval-augmented generation. COT (chain of thought) prompting method facilitates logical reasoning by the model on programming problems through prompts. Single-shot retrieval-augmented generation technology enables the construction of query statements based on programming issues to retrieve information from external knowledge bases. Meanwhile, dynamic retrieval-augmented generation technology allows for real-time retrieval from external knowledge bases during the code generation process, integrating retrieved documents to continue generating subsequent code. However, these methods primarily address the hallucination problem in code generation from a localized perspective. To simultaneously resolve issues such as reasoning errors, inadequate overall knowledge, and insufficient localized knowledge in the field of code generation, this study introduces the Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation framework based on Dynamic Revision of Thoughts (RACGDRT). The core concept of this framework involves firstly enabling the large model to produce a comprehensive code draft (utilizing COT prompts), followed by conducting error detection on code segments corresponding to different reasoning steps within the draft. Upon detecting an error, the Keyword Extractor (KE) will extract keywords and formulate query statements for both the user’s input question and the erroneous code segment, subsequently retrieving pertinent documents from the external knowledge base. Finally, with the retrieved documents and questions in hand, the large model proceeds to iteratively generate the next code draft. RACG-DRT guarantees the rationality of reasoning via COT, constructs query statements tailored to erroneous thought segments and issues to bolster both local and holistic knowledge, and iteratively produces code drafts to uphold the integrity of the code generation process.

column6: DiagAgent: An Agent Framework for Power Equipment Fault Diagnosis by Integrating RAG and MCP Tools
column7: Large language models (LLMs) show promise for diagnosing power equipment faults. However, they face issues such as hallucinations, knowledge lag, and a lack of specialized analytical capabilities. This paper introduces DiagAgent, an innovative Artificial Intelligence (AI) agent framework. It synergizes Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with domainspecific small models through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). The framework first constructs a knowledge base containing equipment information and historical cases. Next, it employs a multi-level hybrid retrieval strategy to obtain relevant information as the intelligent core. The LLM then dynamically invokes specialized small-model tools encapsulated via MCP, which include analyzers for operating data, $\text{SF}_{6}$ pressure, and simulations, to conduct in-depth analysis. Finally, it generates structured diagnostic reports. A power bushing diagnosis case, implemented on the Dify platform, demonstrates that DiagAgent significantly outperforms baseline methods, achieving a diagnostic accuracy of 91.3% and a report quality score of $4.4 / 5$. This work provides a practical and scalable blueprint for developing reliable, domain-specific AI assistants in the power industry and beyond.

column6: Enhancing Commit Message Generation in Software Repositories: A RAG-Based Approach
column7: Creating clear and detailed commit messages manually is both time-consuming and prone to inconsistency. Existing automated methods, such as rule-based templates, retrieval-based systems, and neural sequence-to-sequence models, often fail to capture the full context of code changes, resulting in incomplete or inaccurate messages. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework that combines a pretrained retriever with transformer-based generators (BART and T5). Our approach builds a comprehensive knowledge base of code diffs and commit messages, incorporating relevant external context through joint end-to-end training. The dataset was sourced from the top GitHub repositories and curated using three key filtering and cleaning steps: (1) excluding non-target programming languages via regular expressions, (2) detecting the presence of “What” and “Why” information in commit messages with a Bidirectional LSTM model, and (3) manually evaluating high-quality messages with expert assistance. Experiments on curated datasets in Python, JavaScript, and Java demonstrate that our BART-based configuration significantly improves BLEU, METEOR, and ROUGE scores compared to existing methods, with the RAG-based models consistently outperforming other approaches across all evaluation metrics.
